ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the position of the line $y=kx+b$ in the Cartesian coordinate system is illustrated. What is the solution set for the inequality $kx+b\le 2$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} According to the graph, the line $y=kx+b$ passes through the points (0,1) and (2,0),\\
Substituting these two points into $y=kx+b$ yields $\left\{\begin{array}{l}b=1\\ 2k+b=0\end{array}\right.$, \\
Solving this system gives $\left\{\begin{array}{l}b=1\\ k=-\frac{1}{2}\end{array}\right.$, \\
$\therefore$ the equation of the line is: $y=-\frac{1}{2}x+1$, \\
Substituting y=2 we get $2=-\frac{1}{2}x+1$, \\
This gives x=$-2$, \\
$\therefore$ the solution set of the inequality $kx+b\le 2$ is $\boxed{x\ge -2}$.
